• --kv-cache-memory-bytes — cap KV cache by bytes precisely
  • --max-num-seqs — concurrency cap, indirectly bounded by this arg
  • --kv-cache-dtype — KV quantization, effectively enlarges the pool

docs.title: --kv-cache-dtype
docs.text:
KV cache storage dtype — directly determines KV bytes per token; the #1 lever for trading precision for concurrency.

Property Value Type str (CacheDType) Default "auto" (follows model dtype) Category Scheduling & Memory

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Data type for kv cache storage. If "auto", will use model data type. CUDA 11.8+ supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3) and fp8_e5m2. ROCm (AMD GPU) supports fp8 (=fp8_e4m3). Intel Gaudi (HPU) supports fp8 (using fp8_inc). Some models (namely DeepSeekV3.2) default to fp8, set to bfloat16 to use bfloat16 instead...

(vLLM source: CacheConfig.cache_dtype, cache.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The quantization target is the KV cache, not the weights: the two are independent. Weight quantization is controlled by --quantization; this arg controls the storage format of the K/V tensors during attention. fp8 KV halves bytes per token vs bf16 — effectively doubling the KV pool.

Three points from the source docstring:

  1. auto = follow the model weight dtype;
  2. Some models default to fp8 (the source names DeepSeekV3.2) — on those, pass bfloat16 explicitly to opt out;
  3. Explicit fp16/bfloat16 must match the model dtype, otherwise an error is raised;
  4. Platform backends can register custom KV dtypes via register_kv_cache_dtype — Ascend fp8/int8 KV support uses this mechanism.

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Related arg Relationship --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype Ascend-side C8 derivation pair: since v0.30.0, the C8 layout of SFA sparse-attention models is derived from this arg (cache_dtype ∈ {fp8, int8}), while the Lightning-Indexer sparse layers' C8 layout is derived from indexer_kv_dtype ∈ {fp8, int8} — official tutorials set both together (e.g. --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8); P and D sides must use identical values --gpu-memory-utilization KV quantization = effectively enlarging the pool; both stack --block-size commonly configured together in official tutorials (fp8 + block 32) --max-num-seqs a bigger pool means less preemption at the same concurrency Weight NZ (weight_nz_mode) don't confuse: that one is for weights, this one is KV cache Ascend-derived flags since v0.30.0, cache_dtype ∈ {fp8, int8} derives enable_sparse_sfa_c8 on SFA models; cache_dtype == turboquant_4bit_nc derives enable_sparse_sfa_turboquant

The memory math: KV tokens that fit ≈ pool capacity ÷ (2 × layers × KV heads × head dim × bytes per element). kv-cache-dtype fp8 drops "bytes per element" from 2 to 1 — capacity ×2.

docs.title: Tuning guidance
docs.text: Scenario Suggestion MoE large models, long context (mainstream official pattern) fp8 (see the DeepSeek-V4-Pro recipe); validate precision regression Precision-sensitive auto / bfloat16; free memory via other levers Mamba/SSM models the counterpart is --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype, default auto

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Explicit values in official tutorials:
  • fp8 — DeepSeek-V4-Pro: --kv-cache-dtype fp8 with --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8
  • int8 / mxfp8 — see the patched value domain below
  • The precision/memory tradeoff is explicit: fp8 KV halves memory, but validate accuracy for your workload.

docs.title: Ascend-patched values (int8 / mxfp8)
docs.text:
The upstream CacheDType values (auto / fp8 / fp8_e5m2 / fp8_e4m3 / bf16 / fp16…) do not include int8. vLLM-Ascend appends two Ascend-only values to the CacheConfig.cache_dtype Literal via the platform patch patch/platform/patch_kv_cache_dtype.py — the same --kv-cache-dtype arg gains two extra legal values on Ascend:

Patched value Meaning Applies to int8 KV cache stored in int8 MLA KV cache of DeepSeek V4-style sparse MLA models; derives enable_sparse_sfa_c8 on SFA models (since v0.30.0) mxfp8 C8-MXFP layout: FP8 KV + E8M0 scales A5-chip QFA path (verbatim from the patch header: "the A5 QFA path"); the C8-MXFP backend requires 512-token pages

Patch mechanics: it rewrites the Literal in three places (the module symbol CacheDType, the class annotation, the dataclass field type) and then calls rebuild_dataclass(force=True) to regenerate the pydantic schema; on main it also appends both values to the KV_CACHE_DTYPES mirror list (read by the is_known_kv_cache_dtype validator), and CLI choices are widened in platform.py::pre_register_and_update; worker processes re-apply it via patch/worker/patch_kv_cache_dtype.py. The patch is idempotent.

Trap: outside the Ascend environment these two values are illegal — the validation logic is injected at plugin activation, so vLLM's official docs never mention them. v0.30.0's derive_and_validate already consumes int8 (cache_dtype in ["fp8", "int8"] deriving SFA-C8), i.e. the int8 domain has been legal at least since v0.30.0.

The companion patch patch/platform/patch_indexer_kv_dtype.py does the same for --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype: the upstream Literal is auto / bf16 / fp8 / mxfp4 / nvfp4, and the patch appends int8 (DeepSeek V4 Ascend indexer K cache). This is also the precondition for indexer_kv_dtype ∈ {fp8, int8} deriving LI-C8 since v0.30.0.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 32

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --quantization — weight quantization (independent of this arg)
  • --block-size — commonly configured together
  • --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype — the Mamba-family counterpart

docs.title: --kv-transfer-config
docs.text:
KV transfer configuration (JSON) — the core parameter of PD (Prefill/Decode) disaggregation: how KV moves between nodes.

Property Value Type KVTransferConfig (JSON) Default None (disabled) Category KV Transfer & PD

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
The config corresponding to the KV transfer... defines the KV connector and its transport properties.

(vLLM source: KVTransferConfig, config/kv_transfer.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
What PD disaggregation is: prefill (heavy compute) and decode (long generation) are split into separate node pools. A prefill node computes a request's full KV, then sends the KV through the KV transfer layer to a decode node, which resumes generation. Each pool scales with its own load.

This parameter's role: tells the engine "is this node a KV producer or consumer, which connector, which transport". Key JSON fields (evidenced from official tutorials):

Field Role kv_connector connector implementation (below) kv_role this node's role: kv_producer (prefill side) / kv_consumer (decode side)

Connectors used in official tutorials (by frequency):

Connector Where MooncakeConnectorV2 PD disaggregation Mooncake tutorial etc. — current default recommendation MooncakeConnectorV1 earlier Mooncake deployments AscendStoreConnector Ascend-native KV pooling (KV Cache Pool / Ascend Store) MultiConnector multi-connector composition

docs.title: KV pooling (Ascend Store)
docs.text:
KV pooling (KV Cache Pool / Ascend Store) is vLLM-Ascend's cross-node KV cache pooling storage: KV cache is written to external storage backends and shared/reused across multiple vLLM instances under the PD disaggregation architecture, avoiding redundant prefill of identical prefixes. It is configured through this arg's AscendStoreConnector — not an additional-config flag, which is why "pooling" yields no hit in the feature-flags overview.

Backend When to choose (official docs) Mooncake Default backend; pick it for SSD Offload (extended KV capacity) or multi-tenant quota management Memcache Based on MemFabric; pick it for A3 HCCS low-latency transfer or layer-by-layer KV transfer (use_layerwise) Yuanrong Based on openyuanrong-datasystem; pick it for multi-node deployment, Remote H2D transfer, or openEuler integration

Key constraints (official feature page):

  • Supported since vLLM-Ascend v0.23.0; hardware A2 / A3 / 950PR&950DT;
  • use_layerwise layer-wise transfer is supported only on the prefill node of the Mooncake / Memcache backends;
  • kv_load_failure_policy=recompute does not yet support hybrid-attention models (e.g. DeepSeekV4, Qwen 3.5);
  • Mooncake backend requires >= 0.3.11.post1 (layer-wise needs >= 0.3.14); Memcache backend requires memfabric-hybrid / memcache-hybrid >= 1.3.0;
  • Combines with enable_kvpp (pooling uses kv_role = kv_producer / kv_both with whole-block loading); Mooncake layerwise pooling (backend="mooncake" + use_layerwise=true) is Experimental.

Official details: KV Cache Pool (Ascend Store) · Mooncake layerwise pooling adaptation

docs.title: Anatomy of a typical pooling config (PD disaggregation + Memcache pooling)
docs.text:
The standard form in the official GLM5.2/5.3 tutorials: MultiConnector combines point-to-point transfer + pooling write. Field-by-field meanings below; for the verbatim command see the official tutorial.

Top-level fields

Field Meaning kv_connector: "MultiConnector" Combiner: binds the connectors listed under connectors into one config, so the same KV travels multiple paths at once engine_id Engine instance ID, distinguishing co-located engines (the second prefill engine uses "1" in the official example) kv_role: "kv_producer" This node's role: the prefill side is the producer; the decode side uses kv_consumer kv_port Transfer port

Connector 1 MooncakeConnectorV2 — P2P transfer (the "now": this request's KV goes to decode)

Field Meaning use_ascend_direct: true Enable Ascend direct transfer: KV cache passes NPU-to-NPU without host-memory staging prefill: {dp_size, pp_size, tp_size, pp_layer_partition} Declares the prefill-side parallel topology (e.g. "42,36" = 78 layers split into two PP stages) for per-layer KV mapping decode: {dp_size, tp_size} Declares the decode-side topology; P and D shard differently, so KV is re-sliced to the peer's shape

Connector 2 AscendStoreConnector — pooling write (the "future": prefix-hit requests skip prefill)

Field Meaning backend: "memcache" Pool backend choice: memcache (MemFabric-based, for A3 HCCS low-latency) / mooncake / yuanrong use_layerwise false = whole-block pooling (this example); true = layer-wise transfer (GLM5.2 1M long-context variant; prefill node of Mooncake/Memcache backends only) lookup_rpc_port Local IPC endpoint ID between the pooling-scheduler process and the worker; independently launched services sharing one RPC base directory must use distinct values

Analogy: MultiConnector is like courier "direct delivery + warehousing" — MooncakeConnectorV2 is the rider delivering this parcel right now, while AscendStoreConnector simultaneously files it into the shared warehouse, so the next identical order ships straight from stock.

docs.title: Full example: PD disaggregation + Memcache pooling (prefill node)
docs.text:
vllm serve <MODEL_PATH> \
  --kv-transfer-config '{
    "kv_connector": "MultiConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_producer",
    "engine_id": "0",
    "kv_port": "30000",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "connectors": [
        {
          "kv_connector": "MooncakeConnectorV2",          # 1) P2P transfer: KV straight to decode
          "kv_role": "kv_producer",
          "kv_port": "30000",
          "kv_connector_extra_config": {
            "use_ascend_direct": true,                     # NPU-to-NPU direct path
            "prefill": {"dp_size": 1, "pp_size": 2, "tp_size": 16, "pp_layer_partition": "42,36"},
            "decode":  {"dp_size": 16, "tp_size": 2}        # topology per your deployment
          }
        },
        {
          "kv_connector": "AscendStoreConnector",          # 2) pooling write: KV into the memcache pool
          "kv_role": "kv_producer",
          "kv_connector_extra_config": {
            "backend": "memcache",
            "use_layerwise": false,                        # false=whole-block; 1M long-context variant uses true
            "lookup_rpc_port": "0"                         # distinct per co-located service
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }'

📌 Source: official GLM5.2 tutorial, MemCache KV pooling section (abridged). Topology values (pp/tp/dp and layer partition) vary by deployment — the verbatim command and the decode-side config are governed by the official doc.

How to read this command: first check kv_role to confirm this is the prefill node → the two connectors in MultiConnector.connectors each do one job → cross-reference each connector's kv_connector_extra_config against the three field tables above.

Combination with feature flags: the official GLM5.2 pooling example also passes --additional-config '{"enable_cpu_binding": true, "recompute_scheduler_enable": true, "enable_dsa_cp": true, "enable_flashcomm1": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 1}' — PD pooling deployments are commonly combined with recompute scheduling, DSA CP (v0.30.0; replaced by PCP on main) and FlashComm1.

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Related arg Relationship --enable-prefix-caching explicitly disabled under PD (--no-enable-prefix-caching, official tutorial practice) — prefix-reuse semantics are owned by the transfer layer --prefill-context-parallel-size only MooncakeConnectorV1/V2 are fully PCP-compatible (official matrix) --block-size KV block layout must align with the transfer layer Ascend recompute_scheduler_enable / dyntra_lb_config recomputation scheduling and dynamic load balancing for PD

Analogy: PD disaggregation is a "central kitchen + front stores" model — the kitchen (prefill pool) cooks everything to half-done (KV computed), this parameter is the cold-chain logistics protocol (which warehouse, which truck, which store), and the stores (decode pool) only do the final plating.

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Official PD tutorials set companion env vars first (Mooncake address, local KV pool path), then pass this arg; verbatim commands and env-var setup are in the official docs (Mooncake single-node deployment).
  • When combined with PCP, connector choice is constrained (table above); re-verify compatibility after each vllm-ascend upgrade.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# decode node example (simplified from the official tutorial)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV2","kv_role":"kv_consumer",...}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --enable-prefix-caching — explicitly disabled under PD
  • --prefill-context-parallel-size — long-context PD
  • recompute_scheduler_enable — Ascend PD recomputation scheduling

docs.title: --max-model-len
docs.text:
Maximum context length served by the model (prompt + output) — requests beyond it are rejected outright.

Property Value Type int (accepts k/m/g/t suffix shorthand) Default None (auto-derived from the model config) Category Scheduling & Memory

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Model context length (prompt and output). If unspecified, will be automatically derived from the model config.

(vLLM source: ModelConfig.max_model_len, model.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Two paths:

  1. Unset: takes the context limit from the model config (the exact source field varies by model — max_position_embeddings, rope-derived values, etc. — whatever the actual config provides);
  2. Set explicitly: becomes a service-level hard cap. Requests exceeding it are rejected at admission (an error says the sequence is too long) and never reach the scheduler.

k/m/g/t suffix shorthand: vLLM's CLI layer expands bare numeric suffixes (human_readable_int); the same expansion is applied inside JSON-valued args by _expand_json_human_readable_numbers:

Form Meaning Result --max-model-len 128k lowercase = decimal 128000 --max-model-len 128K uppercase = binary 131072

⚠️ Case matters: lowercase k/m/g/t are powers of 10; uppercase K/M/G/T are powers of 2. Mind the case in configs.

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Versus KV cache capacity: a sequence's peak memory need ≈ max_model_len × KV bytes per token. This parameter is therefore the first input to KV pool planning: the pool must hold at least a few sequences near max_model_len, or effective concurrency collapses toward zero.

Startup validation against max_num_batched_tokens (scheduler.py verify_max_model_len):

chunked prefill off: max_num_batched_tokens < max_model_len → startup error

Reason: without chunking, a single prefill must complete in one step, so the budget must fit the longest sequence. With chunked prefill on, the constraint is lifted — which is why nearly all long-context deployments enable it.

Preemption linkage: a larger max_model_len means more KV per sequence at worst case; mixed long/short traffic fills the pool sooner and raises vllm:num_preemptions. Shrinking it is the most direct way to trade context for concurrency.

docs.title: Tuning guidance
docs.text: Scenario Suggestion Long-document / agent workloads Set to business max input + max output; rejecting overlong requests beats letting one giant sequence degrade everyone Tight memory Shrink this first (caps per-request peak), then concurrency Aligning with official recipes Copy the value from the model's official tutorial (below) — safest baseline

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Nearly all official tutorials set it explicitly (it is the #1 driver of KV cache memory pressure):
  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash / GLM5.3-Flash / Kimi-K3.1-Pro: 1048576 (1M)
  • GLM5 / Kimi-K3: 131072
  • Also 133120, 135168, 40000, etc., trimmed per model
  • Long prefills on Ascend can be further split across ranks with prefill-context-parallel-size (see its compatibility matrix).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 131072
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-model-len 128K   # 131072

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --max-num-batched-tokens — startup constraint when chunked prefill is off
  • --enable-chunked-prefill — the key that lifts the constraint
  • --prefill-context-parallel-size — multi-card prefill acceleration for long contexts
  • --gpu-memory-utilization — source of the KV pool capacity

docs.title: --max-num-batched-tokens
docs.text:
Max tokens processed per iteration — the core knob for prefill chunking and batch scheduling.

Property Value Type int Default None (auto, resolved by device memory tier and usage context — see below) Category Scheduling & Memory

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Maximum number of tokens that can be processed in a single iteration.

(vLLM source: EngineArgs.max_num_batched_tokens, arg_utils.py / SchedulerConfig.max_num_batched_tokens, scheduler.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Where it sits in the scheduling pipeline: it is the per-step token budget. The scheduler packs RUNNING requests into the batch against this budget: prefill requests are chunked to fit the remaining budget (chunked prefill), decode requests take at least 1 token each per step. Packing stops when the budget is exhausted.

Division of labor with max_num_seqs: max_num_seqs caps how many sequences; max_num_batched_tokens caps how many tokens in total. An 8000-token prompt can prefill in one step (budget permitting) or be split across 4 steps at a budget of 2000 — that chunk size is this parameter.

Default resolution (when omitted from the CLI; resolved by get_batch_defaults(); columns are the offline LLM class vs the API server usage context):

Device memory LLM (offline) OpenAI API server ≥ 160 GB (B200/B300 etc.) 16384 16384 ≥ 70 GB and not A100 (H100/H200 etc.) 16384 8192 Everything else 8192 2048 batched-DP MoE path 256 (DEFAULT_MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS_FOR_BATCHED_DP) same

Subsequent corrections when the user did not set it (arg_utils.py _set_default_max_num_seqs_and_batched_tokens_args):

  1. performance_mode = "throughput" → doubled;
  2. chunked prefill off → max(resolved, max_model_len) (so a single sequence fits);
  3. clamp: min(max_num_seqs × max_model_len, resolved).

The scheduler may issue even fewer tokens: max_num_scheduled_tokens (the true per-step emission cap) "is usually equal to max_num_batched_tokens, but can be smaller in cases when the model might append tokens into the batch (such as speculative decoding)" (scheduler.py field docstring).

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Hard constraint with max_num_seqs (startup validation, scheduler.py verify_max_model_len):

max_num_batched_tokens ≥ max_num_seqs    (refuses to start otherwise)

The logic is plain: every sequence needs at least 1 token per step, so the count can never exceed the token budget.

Interplay with max_model_len: with chunked prefill on, long prompts are chunked, so max_num_batched_tokens may be far below max_model_len; with chunked prefill off, max_num_batched_tokens < max_model_len is a startup error. In other words: to run long contexts on a small budget, chunked prefill must be on.

Preemption linkage: a larger budget advances more long requests per step (faster KV consumption); a smaller budget stretches long requests over more steps (slower per-step KV growth, longer queues). Either imbalance shows up as a rising vllm:num_preemptions.

Ascend-specific: with enable_prefill_mc2 on, max_num_batched_tokens feeds the mc2_token_capacity calculation; officially recommended ≤ tp_size × 512 in that scenario (additional_config reference).

docs.title: Tuning guidance
docs.text: Goal How TTFT-sensitive Set slightly above the typical prompt length so a single prefill finishes in one step TPOT-sensitive Shrink it so large prefills don't crowd out decode steps; pair with chunked prefill for smooth mixing Throughput first Raise it (mind the ≥ max_num_seqs constraint); performance_mode=throughput doubles the default CPP dynamic chunking Sweep the fixed-chunk optimum in [8192, 16384, 24576, 32768] first; with dynamic chunking on, the optimum is typically 2–4× the fixed-chunk value (official CPP guide)

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Typical tutorial values: 1024 (small models) / 10240 / 16384 / 20480 / 32768.
  • DeepSeek-V4-Flash: 10240
  • Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: 20480 (with --max-num-seqs 64)
  • Kimi-K3: 1024
  • This knob is the most sensitive one for CPP (dynamic chunked pipeline parallelism): too large introduces compute waste, too small hurts operator efficiency (the official guide's own words).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-num-batched-tokens 16384

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --max-num-seqs — count cap, must be ≤ this arg
  • --enable-chunked-prefill — this arg is the actual chunk size
  • --max-model-len — with chunked prefill off, this arg must not be below it
  • profiling_chunk_config — Ascend dynamic chunking config

docs.title: --max-num-seqs
docs.text:
Maximum sequences processed in a single iteration — the concurrency gate of the inference engine.

Property Value Type int Default None (auto, resolved by device memory tier — see below) Category Scheduling & Memory

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Maximum number of sequences to be processed in a single iteration.

(vLLM source: EngineArgs.max_num_seqs, arg_utils.py / SchedulerConfig.max_num_seqs, scheduler.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Where it sits in the scheduling pipeline: every scheduler step, the scheduler picks sequences from the RUNNING queue to form a batch; max_num_seqs is the count cap of that batch. It is a hard cap — the scheduler will never exceed it, even if the KV cache could hold more.

It affects more than scheduling — it sizes the runtime itself. The source docstring for the adjacent max_num_active_seqs states it plainly:

max_num_seqs sizes the model runner (per-request buffers and CUDA graph capture) and is also the default admission limit.

So raising it is not free — per-request buffers and CUDA Graph capture memory grow with it. This is also why the capture-size formula below contains it.

What the default actually is (when the CLI flag is omitted, EngineArgs.max_num_seqs = None, resolved by get_batch_defaults() by device memory):

Device memory Resolved value ≥ 160 GB (B200/B300 etc.) 1024 ≥ 70 GB and not A100 (H100/H200 etc.) 1024 Everything else (A100, small-memory devices, probe failure) 256

Two corrections are applied after resolution (same function, arg_utils.py _set_default_max_num_seqs_and_batched_tokens_args):

  1. With performance_mode = "throughput", both auto defaults are doubled (throughput mode only);
  2. Final clamp: max_num_seqs = min(max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens) — a step can never hold more sequences than tokens.

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Picture the engine as a factory:

Parameter Factory analogy Dimension controlled Default (vLLM main) --max-num-seqs Workpieces on the line at once Count: per-step concurrent sequence cap 256 / 1024 (memory tier) --max-num-batched-tokens Material processed per cycle Tokens: per-step compute cap 2048–16384 (tier & usage) --gpu-memory-utilization Factory floor area Memory: source of the KV cache pool size 0.92 / 1.0 (extensible KV) --max-model-len Max size of one workpiece Length: per-sequence context cap auto-derived from model config

The core formula — effective concurrency:

effective concurrency ≈ min(max_num_seqs, KV cache pool capacity ÷ average context length)

The KV pool capacity comes from gpu-memory-utilization (device memory minus weights and activations). Even with a huge max_num_seqs, if the KV pool cannot hold the contexts, concurrency stalls — extra requests queue, or get preempted.

Two startup validations enforced in source (SchedulerConfig.verify_max_model_len; violation = refuse to start):

  1. max_num_batched_tokens < max_num_seqs → error: "max_num_batched_tokens must be greater than or equal to max_num_seqs" (each sequence needs at least one token per step);
  2. With chunked prefill off, max_num_batched_tokens < max_model_len → error, asking you to raise the former or lower the latter.

Preemption linkage: when the KV pool is full and new tokens have nowhere to go, the scheduler pauses (swaps out) some RUNNING requests — that is preemption. It is the runtime symptom of the formula above breaking: concurrency × average context length persistently exceeding the KV pool. vLLM exposes the vllm:num_preemptions metric (v1/metrics/loggers.py). A non-zero value means overload — lower concurrency or grow the KV pool instead of adding more load.

Fine-grained TP interplay (Ascend-specific, Fine_grained_TP guide): the largest cudagraph capture size must cover

min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens))

otherwise oproj/mlp fine-grained TP is auto-disabled with a warning at startup (and max_cudagraph_capture_size also truncates it).

docs.title: Tuning guidance
docs.text: Goal How Watch Throughput Raise max_num_seqs (keep max_num_batched_tokens ≥ max_num_seqs); give enough memory vllm:num_preemptions should be 0; non-zero = overload Low latency Lower max_num_seqs to shorten queues; set max_num_batched_tokens slightly above the typical prompt length TTFT / TPOT OOM / tight memory Lower this arg or relieve gpu_memory_utilization pressure; or use quantized weights / smaller max_model_len Startup profiling logs

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Observed tutorial values span 12 / 16 / 32 / 64 / 128, depending on HBM size, model scale, and TTFT/TPOT targets.
  • Kimi-K3: 12
  • Qwen3.5-397B-A17B: 64 (with --max-num-batched-tokens 20480)
  • GLM5.2 / Qwen3.5-27B family: 128
  • Note Ascend tutorials almost always set this explicitly (12–128), generally below the 1024 the large-memory GPU tier would resolve to — don't trust the default on NPU; start from the official tutorial values and tune by measurement.
  • Affects balancing granularity when dynamic EPLB / balance scheduling is on.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --max-num-seqs 32

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --max-num-batched-tokens — co-determines per-step compute; must be ≥ this arg
  • --gpu-memory-utilization — KV pool size, indirectly bounds effective concurrency
  • --max-model-len — per-sequence length cap, directly tied to preemption
  • --compilation-config — the capture-size formula includes this arg

docs.title: --pipeline-parallel-size
docs.text:
Pipeline parallel (PP) group count — spreading the model's layers across devices, for when a model doesn't fit on one machine.

Property Value Type int Default 1 Category Parallelism

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Number of pipeline parallel groups.

(vLLM source: ParallelConfig.pipeline_parallel_size, parallel.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
What gets sliced, and how data flows: TP slices inside each layer; PP slices between layers. The model is divided into layer stages, one per device; a micro-batch flows through the stages like an assembly line, with different devices working on different micro-batches at the same time.

Two costs:

  1. Pipeline bubbles: devices idle waiting for the previous stage's output; bubble fraction grows with stage count;
  2. Scheduling complexity: the batch must be split into rotating micro-batches.

Source hard constraint (model.py):

PP > 1 requires the model to implement the SupportsPP interface,
otherwise NotImplementedError: "Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model."

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Related arg Relationship --tensor-parallel-size world size = TP × PP; stack PP only when one node can't hold the model --data-parallel-size DP/PP compose; large-scale MoE commonly uses TP×PP×DP Ascend profiling_chunk_config CPP dynamic chunking exists specifically to optimize micro-batch splitting for PP, easing bubbles

Analogy: PP is a factory assembly line — each station (device) owns a fixed set of processes (layers), and products (micro-batches) flow through. More stations don't always mean faster: conveyor idle time (bubbles) eats the gains. Add stations only when one station can't finish a product alone.

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Tutorial values: 1 / 2 / 4: enabled for super-large multi-node deployments (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro).
  • Ascend's CPP (dynamic chunked pipeline parallelism) is the dedicated PP optimization: per-step token splitting of micro-batches is tuned to device load; the tuning target is --max-num-batched-tokens (search space [8192, 16384, 24576, 32768]; the dynamic-chunking optimum is typically 2–4× the fixed-chunk value).
  • Rule of thumb: don't enable PP if the model fits on one node (pure bubble loss); when it doesn't fit, PP is mandatory — and CPP above it recovers some bubble loss.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --pipeline-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 8

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --tensor-parallel-size
  • --data-parallel-size
  • profiling_chunk_config — Ascend's dedicated PP optimization

docs.title: --prefill-context-parallel-size
docs.text:
Prefill Context Parallel (PCP): splits a long request's prefill tokens across ranks to cut TTFT.

Property Value Type int Default 1 Category Parallelism

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Prefill Context Parallel (PCP) splits the prefill tokens of a long prefill request across additional ranks. Each rank computes a different part of the sequence, reducing time to first token (TTFT).

(vLLM-Ascend official context parallel guide; upstream concept: vLLM Context Parallel Deployment)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Difference from TP: TP slices "each layer's matrices" (every token passes through a slice on every device); PCP slices "one sequence" (different devices compute different segments of the same sequence, with cross-device exchange at attention layers). TP reduces per-layer compute; PCP reduces the latency of a single prefill — a long request that one device would compute serially is now split N-ways.

Division of labor with DCP: PCP accelerates prefill; --decode-context-parallel-size (DCP) shards KV by decode groups, reducing duplicate KV storage and lifting decode throughput. The two can stack and share the same devices.

Current status: PCP is experimental on vLLM-Ascend (the official guide's own words).

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Official compatibility matrix (Ascend context parallel guide; A2/A3 MLA fully compatible):

Combination Compatibility Basic PCP on MLA / GQA ✅ Prefix caching / chunked prefill / PD disaggregation (MooncakeConnectorV1/V2) + PCP ✅ fully compatible Graph mode + PCP Partial (FULL mode unsupported) Speculative decoding + PCP Partial: MLA → MTP only, GQA → Eagle3 only Sequence parallelism (SP) + PCP ✅ (this is DSA-PCP, the MRv2-recommended path)

Source hard constraint (DCP side, model.py):

DCP > 1 on a non-MLA (GQA/MQA) model: tensor_parallel_size must exceed the total KV head count,
dcp_size ≤ TP // num_kv_heads, and Q-heads-per-KV-head % dcp_size == 0

Expert sharding: PCP is the second factor of the MoE expert sharding product TP × PCP × DP — enabling PCP also changes per-rank expert counts.

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Tutorial values: 1 / 2 / 8, often stacked with --decode-context-parallel-size.
  • DSA-PCP (PCP + sequence parallelism) is the recommended long-context path on Ascend MRv2, replacing the legacy env-var switch enable_context_parallel.
  • While experimental, re-verify the compatibility table after each vllm-ascend upgrade.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --prefill-context-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 4

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --decode-context-parallel-size — decode-phase KV sharding
  • --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size — KV interleave granularity in CP
  • --tensor-parallel-size — upper bound for DCP
  • --data-parallel-size — the third expert-sharding factor

docs.title: --quantization
docs.text:
Weight quantization method — determines weight memory footprint and the compute kernel. Ascend repos use dedicated quantization format naming.

Property Value Type str (QuantizationMethods) Default None (inferred from the model config) Category Model & Loading

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Method used to quantize the weights. If None, we first check the quantization_config attribute in the model config file. If that is None, we assume the model weights are not quantized and use dtype to determine the data type of the weights.

(vLLM source: ModelConfig.quantization, model.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The inference chain (per the source docstring):

explicitly set → use the explicit value
None           → if the model config's quantization_config exists → use it
                 else → weights are not quantized; dtype decides the weight type

So in most cases you don't set it manually — a quantized checkpoint carries its own metadata and is auto-detected. Set it explicitly in two cases: the model config lacks quantization info but you're using a quantized checkpoint; or you want to force a specific quantization kernel path.

It's not only about memory: each method maps to a different weight kernel (compute path), with different precision, speed, and hardware support. Available methods on Ascend are strongly tied to the chip generation — follow the model's tutorial.

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Related arg Relationship --dtype weight dtype on the non-quantized path; the quantization method takes over otherwise --kv-cache-dtype weight quantization ≠ KV quantization — independent, but commonly combined (DeepSeek-V4-Pro: ascend weights + fp8 KV) Ascend weight_nz_mode weight NZ format mode, the layout companion for quantized weights Ascend ascend_compilation_config some quantization formats impose graph-mode requirements

The memory math: weight quantization changes the numerator directly — KV pool ≈ total memory × utilization − weights. W8A8 halves weights vs bf16, and everything saved goes to the KV pool.

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Explicit values in official tutorials:
  • ascend — GLM5.2 / DeepSeek-V4 family (Ascend-specific format)
  • deepseek_v4_fp8, mxfp8 — matched to their respective quantized checkpoints
  • Ascend repo naming convention (GLM5.2 tutorial): GLM-5.2-w4a4c8-mxfp4 (950 series, W4A4 MXFP4 mixed precision). A3 and 950 quantization formats are not interchangeable — match the checkpoint to your hardware.
  • Quantized models should also mind KV dtype and weight NZ (table above).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --quantization ascend

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --dtype — dtype choice on the non-quantized path
  • --kv-cache-dtype — KV quantization (independent of this arg)
  • weight_nz_mode — Ascend weight NZ format

docs.title: --speculative-config
docs.text:
Speculative decoding configuration (JSON): a draft model predicts multiple tokens; the target model verifies them in one pass — trading compute for TPOT.

Property Value Type dict[str, Any] (JSON) Default None (disabled) Category Speculative Decoding

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Speculative decoding configuration.

(vLLM source: SpeculativeConfig, config/speculative.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The principle: a decode step produces 1 token from the target model. Speculative decoding lets a lightweight draft model guess num_speculative_tokens tokens first; the target model verifies them in parallel — accepted tokens all land in one step. With a high acceptance rate, one target step does the work of several, and TPOT drops by a multiple.

The costs, accounted honestly:

  • The draft model itself consumes memory and compute (one extra forward per step);
  • Missed guesses are pure waste — low acceptance makes it slower;
  • Scheduling gets complex: each step schedules "draft forward + target verification".

Key JSON fields (evidenced from official tutorials):

Field Role method draft method; Ascend tutorials use dspark (DeepSpark) num_speculative_tokens guesses per step (tutorials commonly 5–7) model draft model path (same as target for self-speculation) draft_tensor_parallel_size draft-side parallelism (may be smaller than the target's) draft_sample_method draft sampling (e.g. greedy) enforce_eager skip graph capture on the draft side (true in the Kimi-K3 recipe)

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Scheduler-level linkage (source-level): speculation multiplies per-step token counts by 1 + num_speculative_tokens. The scheduler's max_num_scheduled_tokens "is usually equal to max_num_batched_tokens, but can be smaller in cases when the model might append tokens into the batch (such as speculative decoding)" (scheduler.py field docstring).

Graph-capture linkage: capture-size enumeration must cover 1 + n shapes — the fine-grained TP formula min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_num_seqs × (1 + num_speculative_tokens)) contains it (Fine_grained_TP guide).

PCP compatibility (Ascend context parallel guide): MLA + PCP supports MTP drafts only; GQA + PCP supports Eagle3 only.

Ascend companion flags:

Flag Role dynamic_spec_config dynamically tune speculation by acceptance rate enable_flashcomm1 MRv1 speculation communication optimization rejection_sampler_config verification sampling config for RL rollouts

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Recommended method in official tutorials: dspark (DeepSpark).
  • DeepSeek-V4-Pro: --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":5,"method":"dspark"}'
  • Kimi-K3: dspark + draft_tensor_parallel_size:8 + draft_sample_method:"greedy" + num_speculative_tokens:7, with enforce_eager:true on the draft side
  • Often combined with --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --compilation-config — capture sizes must cover speculative shapes
  • --max-num-seqs — the other input to the capture-size formula
  • dynamic_spec_config — Ascend dynamic speculation

docs.title: --tensor-parallel-size
docs.text:
Tensor parallel (TP) group count — the most basic parallelism parameter: slicing each layer's weights across devices.

Property Value Type int Default 1 Category Parallelism

docs.title: Official definition
docs.text:
Number of tensor parallel groups.

(vLLM source: ParallelConfig.tensor_parallel_size, Field(default=1, ge=1), parallel.py)

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
What gets sliced: Q/K/V/output projections of attention and the MLP matmuls are split across devices by head/column. Each device holds a slice of the weights, computes a partial result, and an all-reduce aggregates per layer (twice per layer). The first scaling option when a model doesn't fit on one device.

A hard shape constraint (startup validation, model.py):

total_num_attention_heads % tensor_parallel_size == 0
otherwise: "Total number of attention heads (...) must be divisible by tensor parallel size (...)"

It defines the world size: in arg_utils.py, world_size = pipeline_parallel_size × tensor_parallel_size — total devices = TP × PP, then DP stacks replicas on top.

Mind the KV heads: GQA/MQA models have far fewer KV heads than Q heads. When TP exceeds the KV head count, vLLM replicates KV heads so every device holds at least one (max(1, total_num_kv_heads // tp_size), source comment in model.py get_num_kv_heads) — beyond that point, more TP no longer saves KV memory. For MoE large models, the escape is --enable-expert-parallel + DP.

docs.title: Parameter interplay
docs.text:
Related arg Relationship --pipeline-parallel-size world size = TP × PP; their product sets per-node/cluster device count --data-parallel-size MoE experts sharded by TP × PCP × DP (vLLM source docstring) --enable-expert-parallel the alternative for MoE: EP slices experts, TP keeps attention only --prefill-context-parallel-size DCP on GQA/MQA requires TP > total KV heads (source validation) --distributed-executor-backend TP across nodes needs ray; single-node mp

Analogy: TP is like cutting every page of a thick book into pieces handed to several people reading simultaneously — faster, but every page turn requires a reconciliation (all-reduce).

docs.title: Ascend context & official usage
docs.text:
• Tutorial values: 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16:
  • Single-node A2: Qwen3-Dense tp4 with --distributed-executor-backend mp
  • A3 large models: tp8 common; 16 for multi-node
  • Combined with fine-grained TP (finegrained_tp_config), oproj/mlp can use a different degree than attention — at the cost of the cudagraph capture-size constraint (see its formula).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-8B --tensor-parallel-size 4

docs.title: Related args
docs.text:
• --pipeline-parallel-size — the other world-size factor
  • --data-parallel-size — EP scale source
  • --enable-expert-parallel — the MoE memory partner
  • --distributed-executor-backend — single-node mp / multi-node ray

docs.title: Feature Flags Overview
docs.text:
Feature flags are vLLM-Ascend's own config keys, defined in AscendConfig (vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py) and consumed by the Ascend platform plugin only — other backends (GPU/ROCm) have no such concepts.

📚 Want a systematic, problem-driven tour? Start with the Feature Topics page: 9 topics with principle explainers and when-to-enable tables; this page is the per-key quick reference.

Usage: not top-level CLI args; they go inside the --additional-config JSON:

vllm serve <model> --additional-config '{"enable_kvpp": true}'
Feature flags (this page) Engine args Defined by vLLM-Ascend plugin (AscendConfig) Upstream vLLM (arg_utils.py/config/) Form --additional-config '{"key": val}' top-level --key val CLI args Platform Ascend-only Cross-platform Validation AscendConfig pydantic (extra="forbid") vLLM engine validation

Note: some engine-arg values are re-consumed by the Ascend plugin to derive flags (e.g. --kv-cache-dtype fp8 derives enable_sparse_sfa_c8); the two pages cross-link where they meet.

📍 Ascend configuration has 6 entry points in total (CLI args / additional-config / CLI value-domain patches / kv-transfer-config fields / env vars / runtime_config.json) — this page is just one of them. Start from the configuration entry points overview.

The tables below are auto-generated from data/flags/*.yaml by scripts/generate_tables.py. Do not edit them by hand.

Legend: active ｜ deprecated ｜ removed ｜ planned

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
Config key Short name Type Default Status Legacy env var v0.23 / v0.30 / main Hardware Description ascend_compilation_config Ascend compilation config dict {} active — All Ascend graph-compilation config (typed as AscendCompilationConfig). Sub-keys: enable_npugraph_ex (default true), enable_static_kernel (default false, pre-compiles per-batch-size operator binaries for static shapes), enable_super_kernel (new in v0.30.0, inherits enable_static_kernel when omitted), fuse_norm_quant / fuse_qknorm_rope / fuse_muls_add (new in v0.30.0, all default true); v0.23.0 also has fuse_allreduce_rms. Dependency chain super_kernel -> static_kernel -> npugraph_ex with auto-downgrade on unsupported hardware. ascend_fusion_config Fused-operator config dict {} active — All Fused-operator config. Sub-key fusion_ops_gmmswigluquant (default true) controls the GmmSwigluQuant fused operator. Pydantic validation rejects unknown sub-keys. ascend_log_path Ascend log path str "~/ascend/log/vllm_ascend" active — All vLLM-Ascend log output path; defaults to ~/ascend/log/vllm_ascend. ascend_warmup_config Startup warmup config dict {} active — — All Startup warmup configuration that overlaps with weight loading. batch_job_sched_config Batch-job scheduler config dict {} deprecated — — All Config for the batch-job-aware scheduler. Top-level key deprecated since v0.30.0; use scheduler_config.batch_job_sched_config instead. c8_enable_reshape_optim C8 reshape optimization bool false removed — — — All Reshape optimization for LI-C8 (only takes effect when enable_sparse_li_c8 is on). Removed from source since v0.30.0. combine_quant_mode Combine comm quantization int 0 active — — All Communication quantization mode for the fused combine op, passed as comm_quant_mode to npu_moe_distribute_combine_v2. See operator docs for valid values. draft_window_size Draft KV sliding window int "None" active — — All Draft KV sliding window for speculative decoding: caps only the draft model's attention to the most recent N tokens while the target model keeps full context, leaving output quality unchanged. Works with eagle3/dflash/dspark; for long contexts where the draft's acceptance collapses beyond its trained length. dump_config msprobe inline dump dict None active — All Inline msprobe dump configuration; vLLM-Ascend materializes it to a temporary JSON file passed to the debugger. dump_config_path msprobe dump path str None active — All Path to the msprobe dump configuration file (legacy-compatible option). dynamic_eplb Dynamic expert load balancing bool false active DYNAMIC_EPLB A2, A3 Enable dynamic Expert Parallelism Load Balancer. Part of eplb_config; legacy mode also requires the DYNAMIC_EPLB=true env var as a safety guard. dynamic_spec_config Dynamic spec decoding config dict {} active — — All Configuration for Dynamic Speculative Decoding. dyntra_lb_config DyntraLB load balancing dict {} deprecated — — All DyntraLB load-balancing config for the decode node in P/D disaggregation — configure on the Decode node only. Top-level key deprecated since v0.30.0; use scheduler_config.dyntra_lb_config instead. enable_balance_scheduling Balanced scheduling bool false deprecated VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING All Enable balance scheduling. Top-level key deprecated since v0.30.0 (deprecation warning); use scheduler_config.enable_balance_scheduling instead. enable_context_parallel Context parallel bool false removed VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_CONTEXT_PARALLEL — — — All Enable Context Parallelism. enable_cpu_binding Ascend CPU binding bool true active — All Enable Ascend-native CPU binding on ARM servers. Set to false to disable. enable_dsa_cp DSA context parallel bool false removed — — — All Enable context parallel for DSA attention; mutually exclusive with PCP. Removed on main — enabling it now raises an explicit error telling you to use PCP instead. enable_flashcomm1 FlashComm1 comm optimization bool false active VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1 All Enable FlashComm1 for SP MoE. Model Runner V1 only and requires sequence parallelism; errors on MRv2 — use PCP instead. enable_flashcomm2_parallel_size FlashComm2 parallel size int 0 removed VLLM_ASCEND_FLASHCOMM2_PARALLEL_SIZE — — All FlashComm2 parallel size; 0 disables it. enable_force_eplb Force round-robin expert routing bool false active — — All Force deterministic round-robin expert routing, for profiling only. Replaces real MoE routing so model output/accuracy is invalid — never use in production. enable_fused_mc2 Fused MC2 operator int 0 active VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2 A2, A3, A5 Fused MC2 (MoE dispatch/combine) configuration. On A5, MegaMoe requires SiTU models to expose the CANN MegaMoe wrapper. enable_kv_nz KV NZ layout bool false active — All Enable NZ layout for KV cache; only effective for MLA models such as DeepSeek. enable_kvpp KV layer parallelism (KVPP) bool false active — — All Enable KVPP (KV pipeline parallelism), distributing otherwise-replicated KV caches across TP ranks by layer for non-hybrid MLA/SFA models, so the same HBM fits more context tokens or concurrent requests. Experimental; eager or PIECEWISE graph mode only; for P/D disaggregation enable on the prefill node only. enable_matmul_allreduce Matmul-AllReduce fusion bool false removed VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MATMUL_ALLREDUCE — — All Enable fused Matmul+AllReduce optimization. enable_mc2_hierarchy_comm MC2 cross-node comm bool false deprecated — A2, A3 Enable inter-node RoCE communication for dispatch/combine ops. Deprecated, replaced by mc2_comm_alg="hierarchy". enable_mlapo MLAPO per-layer optimization bool true active VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO All Enable MLAPO (Model Layer-wise Adaptive Parallel Optimization). enable_pcp_embedding_lmhead_weight_sharding PCP embedding/LMHead sharding bool true active — — All When PCP size > 1, shard embedding and LM Head weights across PCP ranks within each TP shard. Incompatible with batch-sharded sampling and fine-grained TP for these modules. enable_pcp_o_proj_weight_sharding PCP O-proj sharding bool true active — — All Whether PCP shards O-projection weights inside the group (SFA-PCP o_proj and DSA-PCP two-stage wo_a/wo_b). Auto-disabled with a warning when unsupported; unused by other attention backends. enable_prefill_mc2 Prefill MC2 reservation bool false active — All Reserve mc2_token_capacity for prefill batches using max_num_batched_tokens. Temporary switch; will be removed once MC2 is complete. enable_shared_expert_dp Shared-expert data parallel bool false active — All Replicate shared-expert weights across TP ranks and run them data-parallel. Improves performance at higher memory cost; independent of upstream MoE sequence parallelism. enable_sparse_li_c8 LI-C8 sparse cache bool false removed — — — All C8 KV cache layout for sparse attention (Lightning Indexer). Settable via additional-config on v0.23.0; derived since v0.30.0 — automatically decided by --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype ∈ {fp8, int8} (requires a sparse-attention model); passing this key has no effect. enable_sparse_sfa_c8 SFA-C8 sparse cache bool false removed — — — All C8 KV cache layout for SFA (Sparse Flash Attention). Settable via additional-config on v0.23.0; derived since v0.30.0 — automatically decided by --kv-cache-dtype ∈ {fp8, int8} (requires an SFA sparse-attention model); passing this key has no effect. enable_transpose_kv_cache_by_block Per-block KV transpose bool true active VLLM_ASCEND_FUSION_OP_TRANSPOSE_KV_CACHE_BY_BLOCK All Whether to enable block-wise transposed KV cache (fused-op path). eplb_config EPLB config dict {} active — A2, A3 EPLB (Expert Parallelism Load Balancer) config. dynamic_eplb enables dynamic balancing; expert_map_record_path records maps; expert_map_path loads static maps. finegrained_tp_config Fine-grained TP config dict {} active — All Configuration for fine-grained tensor parallelism. hamming_sparse Hamming sparse attention dict {"enabled": false, "sparse_json_location": ""} removed — — — All Hamming sparse attention config; dict with enabled and sparse_json_location (path to a real sparse JSON file). Removed from source since v0.30.0. kv_pool_range_debug KV pool audit log bool false active VLLM_ASCEND_KVPOOL_RANGE_DEBUG — All Emit per-layer KVPool ranged-transfer audit events as JSON. Debug only; keep disabled in production to avoid logging overhead. mc2_comm_alg MC2 comm algorithm str "" active — — A2, A3 Communication algorithm for dispatch/combine ops; supersedes enable_mc2_hierarchy_comm. mega_moe_max_tokens MegaMoe token capacity int 65536 active — All Per-rank token capacity after dispatch in the fused MC2/MegaMoe path. Exceeding it may degrade accuracy; tune to actual expert load. mix_placement Mixed expert placement bool false active — All Mixed placement mode (expert/weight placement on the DP×TP plane); counted into the RFork weight-transfer compatibility fingerprint — a sender/receiver mismatch breaks the fingerprint. mlapo_keep_prefill_weights Keep prefill weights bool false active — — All Keep MLAPO prefill weights on kv_consumer (decode-only D nodes) instead of freeing them. Trades NPU memory for stability against local-prefill crashes after weight freeing (issue msmonitor_use_daemon msmonitor daemon mode bool false active MSMONITOR_USE_DAEMON All Whether msmonitor uses daemon mode. multistream_dsv4_dsa_overlap DSV4 DSA multistream overlap bool true active — All Enable DSA multi-stream overlap for DeepSeek V4. multistream_engram_overlap Engram multistream overlap bool "硬件派生（A5 默认 true，其余 false）" active — — All Multistream overlap for the Engram module. Defaults to on only on A5 (FP8-optimized device family); explicit settings override. FULL graphs wait on descriptor-specific external events at consumers, hence the hardware-dependent default. multistream_overlap_gate Multistream gate overlap bool false removed — — — All Enable multistream overlap gating; only effective for MoE models with shared experts. Removed (no source read site since v0.30.0). multistream_overlap_shared_expert Shared-expert multistream overlap bool false active — All Enable multi-stream overlap for the shared expert; only effective on MoE models with shared experts. pa_shape_list PA operator shape list list [] active — All Custom shape list for page-attention ops. profiling_chunk_config Profiling chunk config dict {} deprecated — All Dynamic-chunk pipeline-parallel (profiling chunk) config. Top-level key deprecated since v0.30.0; use scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config instead. recompute_scheduler_enable Recompute scheduler bool false deprecated — All Enable the recompute scheduler. Effective only on the decode node (kv_consumer) of a P/D disaggregation; enabling on a prefill node or PD-mixed mode raises an explicit startup error. Top-level key deprecated since v0.30.0; use scheduler_config.recompute_scheduler_enable instead. mode fails startup with a clear error. refresh Refresh global config bool false active — All Whether to refresh the global Ascend configuration. Usually used by RLHF or ut/e2e tests. rejection_sampler_config Rejection sampler config dict {} active — All Rejection sampler configuration (block verify and entropy verify). rl_config RL mode master switch dict {} active — — All One-click RL mode (enabled: true forces weight_nz_mode=0, VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1, etc.). Sub-keys include sleep_mode_extra_cleanup, enable_training_consistency, enable_batch_invariant. runtime_config Runtime config overlay dict None active — — — All Startup overlay merged into runtime config defaults (detectors, dump quota, report flags). runtime_config_hot_reload Runtime config hot reload bool false active — — — All Enable hot-reload of runtime_config.json (startup-only; not a JSON field). runtime_config_path Runtime Guard path str None active — — — All Path to the Runtime Guard JSON config. Default: /runtime/config/runtime_config.json. runtime_dump_dir KV dump directory str None removed — — — — All Set the KV dump root directory (dump.dump_dir), derived from the report root by default. Removed; use runtime_config.dump.dump_dir instead. runtime_report_dir Report root directory str None removed — — — — All Override the report root directory (default /runtime/report). Removed; use runtime_config.report_dir instead. scheduler_config Scheduler extensions dict {} active — — All Canonical nesting for scheduler extensions: balance scheduling, recompute scheduling, DyntraLB, ShortRequestFirst, dynamic chunked pipeline parallel, etc. Legacy top-level keys still parse but are deprecated. sfa_dcp_force_tmajor_restore SFA DCP T-major restore bool false active — — All Force T-major layout restore for SFA attention under DCP (Decode Context Parallel). Debug/compatibility only — no need to set in normal deployments. short_request_first_config Short-request-first scheduling dict {} deprecated — — All ShortRequestFirst prefill scheduling config for FCFS sync/async, PD-prefill (P) or PD-mixed nodes. Top-level key deprecated since v0.30.0; use scheduler_config.short_request_first_config instead. sparse_kv_offload_config Sparse KV offload dict {} active — — A5 Config for offloading sparse KV cache to DRAM. Sub-keys: enabled, topk_buffer_size (-1 resolves to (1+num_speculative_tokens)*2048), dram_size_per_dp_GB (110), keep_device_kv_cache, use_fused_overlap. 950-series products (A5) only; do not set on prefill nodes. weight_nz_mode Weight NZ mode int 1 active VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ All Weight NZ layout mode. 0 disables NZ, 1 enables for quantized weights only, 2 extends to BF16/FP16 when supported. weight_prefetch_config Weight prefetch config dict {} removed — — — All Weight prefetch config. Removed (no source read site since v0.30.0). xlite_graph_config Xlite graph mode dict {} active — All Configuration for Xlite graph mode.

See the Chinese version for the annotated table. For how to read this table:

  • Config key: the JSON key used in --additional-config. Click through to the detail page.
  • Legacy env var: the environment variable this config migrated from. Since PR #9064 all env vars are migrating to --additional-config; both work during the transition, env vars will be removed in a future release.
  • Hardware: "All" means no chip-specific restriction observed.
  • Description: one-line summary. See each detail page for rationale, examples and risks.
